title: Basic properties of componentwise normalization of a locally Noetherian scheme
statement:
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], and write $
u_X:X^
u	o X$ for its componentwise normalization [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. Then every local ring of $X^
u$ is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], and $
u_X$ is integral [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. The map $
u_X$ induces a bijection between the generic points of irreducible components of $X^
u$ and of $X$ [def-sc-generic-point, def-weil-irreducible-components], and for each generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $X$ the fibre $X^
u	imes_X\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field] is canonically isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\eta)$ over $\kappa(\eta)$. No finiteness of $
u_X$, excellence or reducedness of $X$ is assumed; the empty scheme is allowed.

source.place: Tag 035Q, lemma-normalization-normal (1) and (2); Tag 0CDV, lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components (componentwise description agrees with the normalization when every quasi-compact open has finitely many irreducible components, true for locally Noetherian X); Tag 0BXC, lemma-normalization-birational, proof (generic local rings of X_red and X^nu agree), applied on affine opens; Tag 035P, lemma-description-normalization.

proof.text: Write $X^\nu=\coprod_iY_i$, with $Z_i$ the reduced components and $Y_i=Z_i^\nu$ as in [def-weil-pbc-reduced-normalization]. By [lem-sc-locnoeth-components-locally-finite], an affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ meets only finitely many components: its quasi-compactness gives a finite subcover by neighbourhoods meeting finitely many. By [lem-sc-components-open-injection], the nonempty intersections are distinct components of $U$; they exhaust them because they cover $U$ and an irreducible subset of a finite closed cover lies in one member. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes] and [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identify the reduced intersections with $W_i=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$ for all minimal primes $\mathfrak p_i$ of $A$. For integral $Z_i$, let $\eta_i$ be its unique generic point by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] and put $K_i=\kappa(\eta_i)$. The canonical map of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], composed with $\operatorname{Spec}K_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{Z_i,\eta_i}$ from the residue quotient, gives $h_i:\operatorname{Spec}K_i\to Z_i$. It is quasi-compact (the inverse image of an affine open is empty or a point), and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], since its source is affine. Its pushforward structure sheaf has sections $K_i$ on every nonempty open, since each contains the generic point; hence its relative normalization is the function-field normalization [def-sc-normalization] defining $Y_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](iii) to $h_i$ and the affine open $W_i$ of $Z_i$. This gives $Y_i\times_XU=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$, with $B_i$ the integral closure of $A/\mathfrak p_i$ in $K_i=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_i)$; the field identification is [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra]. Components missing $U$ have empty inverse image.

source.place: Tags 0CDV (lemma-normalization-in-terms-of-components), 035P (lemma-description-normalization); componentwise affine construction, applied to reduced components even when X is nonreduced. Generic-point morphism: Schemes Tag 01J6 (lemma-morphism-from-spec-local-ring) and Equation 02NA (equation-canonical-morphism).

proof.text: For each $i$, the source $\operatorname{Spec}K_i$ of $h_i$ is integral and its only local ring is the field $K_i$, an integrally closed domain. The quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness needed for relative normalization were checked in step 1. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-normal-stalks] to $h_i$ to obtain that all local rings of $Y_i$ are integrally closed domains. Also [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](iv) says $Y_i$ is integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], every summand embeds as an open and closed subscheme; therefore the local ring at a point of $X^\nu$ is exactly its local ring in its unique summand. This proves the asserted normality without assuming that any $Y_i$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 035L (lemma-normal-normalization), integral-source case; Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), proof of (1).

proof.text: For any affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$, step 1 gives finitely many affine inverse-image summands $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], their union is $\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_iB_i)$. Each $B_i$ is integral over $A/\mathfrak p_i$. For $b=(b_i)$ choose a monic equation for each $b_i$ and lift its coefficients to $A$, obtaining $P_i\in A[T]$. Then the monic polynomial $\prod_iP_i$ annihilates $b$, since its $i$-th coordinate has the zero factor $P_i(b_i)$. Hence $A\to\prod_iB_i$ is integral, proving integrality of $\nu_X$ by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. For a point represented by $\mathfrak q\subset A$, choose a component $V(\mathfrak p_i)$ containing it. The integral inclusion $A/\mathfrak p_i\hookrightarrow B_i$ has a prime above $\mathfrak q/\mathfrak p_i$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], giving a point above $\mathfrak q$. Thus $\nu_X$ is surjective. If $U$ is empty, $A=0$ and its inverse image is $\operatorname{Spec}0$; the empty product ring is $0$, integral over $0$ since its only element satisfies the monic polynomial $T$. Surjectivity onto the empty set is vacuous.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), (2), with the affine construction of 035P; Algebra Tag 00GQ (lemma-integral-overring-surjective).

proof.text: Let $\eta_i$ be the generic point of $Z_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization](ii), the factor $\operatorname{Spec}K_i\to Y_i$ of $h_i$ is dominant. Its one-point image therefore has closure all of $Y_i$, so that point is the unique generic point $\xi_i$ of the integral scheme $Y_i$; uniqueness is [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. The factorization of $h_i$ sends $\xi_i$ to $\eta_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], the $Y_i$ are pairwise disjoint, open and closed, and cover $X^\nu$. Any irreducible subset meets at most one of these clopen summands (otherwise its intersections with a summand and its complement separate it); since each $Y_i$ is itself irreducible, these are exactly the irreducible components of $X^\nu$. The distinct $Z_i$ are the components of $X$ by definition, so $\xi_i\mapsto\eta_i$ is the required bijection.

source.place: Tag 035Q (lemma-normalization-normal), (2), via the dominant generic-point maps of Tag 035I (lemma-characterize-normalization).

proof.text: Fix $\eta_j\in U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and put $K=\kappa(\eta_j)=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p_j)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra]. Steps 1 and 3 and [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identify the fibre with $\operatorname{Spec}((\prod_iB_i)\otimes_AK)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-finite-product], the map $\Phi:(\prod_iB_i)\otimes_AK\to\prod_i(B_i\otimes_AK)$, $(b_i)\otimes c\mapsto(b_i\otimes c)_i$, is a module isomorphism. It is a $K$-algebra map: $\Phi(1\otimes c)=(1\otimes c)_i$, and both $\Phi(((b_i)\otimes c)((d_i)\otimes e))$ and $\Phi((b_i)\otimes c)\Phi((d_i)\otimes e)$ equal $(b_id_i\otimes ce)_i$; extend by additivity. For $i\ne j$, choose $s\in\mathfrak p_i\setminus\mathfrak p_j$, possible because distinct minimal primes are incomparable. Its action on $B_i$ is zero and on $K$ is invertible; thus every pure tensor $b\otimes c=(sb)\otimes(c/s)$ is zero. The other factors are therefore zero rings, with empty spectra. For $i=j$, both actions factor through $R=A/\mathfrak p_j$. The identity on pure tensors gives inverse maps between $B_j\otimes_AK$ and $B_j\otimes_RK$: every $r\in R$ lifts to $a\in A$, so the $R$-balancing relation is already an $A$-balancing relation, independently of the lift. Multiplication $b\otimes c\mapsto bc$ has inverse $c\mapsto1\otimes c$: if $b=a/s\in B_j\subset K$ with $a,s\in R$, $s\ne0$, then $b\otimes c=(sb)\otimes(c/s)=1\otimes bc$. Hence the fibre ring is canonically $K$ as a $K$-algebra, so the whole fibre is canonically $\operatorname{Spec}K$ over $K$. The isomorphism is the inverse of the structure map $K\to(\prod_iB_i)\otimes_AK$, which is intrinsic and hence independent of the affine neighbourhood. This calculation uses $A/\mathfrak p_j$, never the false claim that $A_{\mathfrak p_j}$ is a field for nonreduced $A$. For empty $X$ there are no generic points to check.
